newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World Dev may follow SHK anti-speculation move.
newsitem.headline: New World Dev may follow SHK anti-speculation move.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd may follow Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd's anti-speculation flat sale policy if the measure proved to be successful, New World chariman Cheng Yu-tung said on Friday.
"I believe (Sun Hung Kai's) policy is good and we will wait to see the market's response," Cheng told reporters. "If it works fine, we probably will follow."

Sun Hung Kai said this week it would restrict the number of potential buyers registered under limited companies to 20 for every 100 registered buyers on its Tseung Kwan O development in the New Territories, which starts pre-sale in January.
The policy is aimed at reducing property speculation in the wake of widespread concern over a rise in residential property prices, which have risen an average 30 percent this year.
Many speculators are believed to buy flats as limited companies, which allows them to pay less tax and avoid measures restricting quick resale of property.
Cheng said speculative activities were seen to be focused on the luxury residential market and prices for the middle to lower priced flats were still reasonable.
"As developers, we don't want to see speculation on property and every one of us hopes buyers are all end users," he said, adding developers meet the government frequently regarding property prices.
New World director Stewart Leung also said increased demand for luxury residences from overseas also affected prices.
"But speculation is unlikely to spill over to the medium and low price flats since there is enough supply in that area," he said, adding a 15-20 percent rise on flat prices a year was reasonable.

Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Thursday that there was evidence of rampant speculation in the luxury housing market, and expressed concern upward pressure on prices may spread across the entire market.
Leung said he did not agree with the use of administrative measures to curb property prices since that would only trigger overseas' doubts on Hong Kong's policy on economic freedom.
